chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from someone else, from Aban, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that whenever he used to go out from the house, he would say:
"In the Name of Allah I go out, and upon Allah I rely, there is neither Might nor Strength except with Allah."

key_terms.لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّه: There is no might and no strength except with Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for leaving the house in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the Imam’s consistent practice of invoking divine protection and reliance upon leaving the home, a ritual that underscores the integration of spiritual mindfulness into daily routines. The phrase 'no might nor strength except with Allah' (La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah) serves as a theological anchor, affirming that all agency is derived from God, a concept deeply rooted in Shia devotional practice.
